english: Mapandan was established as an independent pueblo through Direction General No. 39, Administration Civil No. 169-C, signed by Governor General Emilio Bravo. The new pueblo was initially composed of the southern barrios of Mangaldan: Payapay, Baloling, Apaya and Amanoaoac.
pangasinan: Nipatindeg so Mapandan bilang bukod ya baley panamegley na Direction General No. 39, Administration Civil No. 169-C, ya pinirmaan nen Gobernador-Heneral Emilio Bravo. Diad gapo, saray barrio ed abalaten na Mangaldan so namporma ed balon baley: Payapay, Baloling, Apaya, tan Amanoaoac.

english: The first center of the new pueblo was in what is now Barangay Torres. The area had abundant pandan plants and was associated with a church where Fr. Jose Torres served as parish priest. However, the location proved inconvenient—too close to the southern boundary and too far from communities to the north.
pangasinan: Say inmunan sentro na balon baley et wala ed lugar ya tatawagen natan ya Barangay Torres. Dakel so tanem ya pandan ed saman ya lugar, tan wala met so simbaan ya nanserbian nen Padre Jose Torres bilang kura paroko. Balet, agmaong so lokasyon lapud asingger ed abalaten ya ketegan tan arawi ed saray komunidad ed amianen.

english: The center was eventually transferred to an area that had previously been a sitio of Apaya. Much of the land in the new Poblacion was owned by the Aquino family. Leon Hilario Aquino encouraged settlement by subdividing land into uniform lots and making them available to families.
pangasinan: Insan, inlipat so sentro na baley ed lugar ya datin sitio na Apaya. Say baleg ya parte na dalin ed balon Poblacion et kayarian na pamilya Aquino. Pinaseseg nen Leon Hilario Aquino iray pamilya ya manayam diman diad impangibingay to ed dalin ed saray lote ya pareho so laknab, tan impangiter to na oportunidad ed saray pamilya.

english: An epidemic severely affected Mapandan, causing major population depletion, residents leaving the town, declining municipal resources, and a financial crisis. The 1903 census recorded Mapandan’s population at 4,198.
pangasinan: Baleg so epekto na epidemya ed Mapandan. Duminmen so bilang na totoo, dakel so nanalis ed baley, duminmen so kayarian tan pondo na munisipalidad, tan nagmaliw ya mabigat so problema ed kuarta. Diad census nen 1903, 4,198 so bilang na totoo ed Mapandan.

english: Because of the population and financial problems caused by the epidemic, Mapandan was temporarily returned to its mother municipality, Mangaldan.
pangasinan: Lapud saray problema ed bilang na totoo tan ed kuarta ya resulta na epidemya, insubli so Mapandan ed sakop na Mangaldan ed agnayag ya panaon.

english: After its restoration, Mapandan developed as a predominantly agricultural community. Farming remained central to the local economy, with rice becoming the municipality’s principal crop. The decades ahead would bring war, occupation, and the beginning of reconstruction.
pangasinan: Kalpasan na impangipawil ed Mapandan bilang bukod ya baley, dinmakel so panagdalus tan panagtanem. Say panagdalus so nanmaliw ya manunan trabaho tan panagmaliw na kuarta ed baley, tan say pagey so nanmaliw ya manunan tanem. Diad saray sinmublay ya dekada, inarap na baley so guerra, okupasyon, tan say pangigapo na panagbangon lamet.

english: Rice became the municipality’s principal crop and livestock raising developed as an important secondary livelihood. The municipality’s current seal still reflects these agricultural foundations through its rice, cattle, chicken and hog imagery.
pangasinan: Say pagey so nanmaliw ya manunan tanem na munisipalidad, tan say panangipaalaga ed saray ayep so nanmaliw ya importante ya arum ni ya panagkabiyagan. Anggad natan, nipanengneng ed selyo na munisipalidad iray pundasyon na agrikultura panamegley na saray larawan na pagey, baka, manok, tan baboy.

english: The Second World War interrupted the development of communities across Pangasinan. In the postwar years, Mapandan’s communities entered a period of reconstruction and social and economic change. The decades following the war also brought changes in landholding, agriculture, education and local community organization.
pangasinan: Say Komadua ya Guerra Mundial so nanpaalangan ed panduruman na saray komunidad ed interon Pangasinan. Diad saray taon kalpasan na guerra, inggapo ed saray komunidad na Mapandan so panagbangon lamet tan saray pananguman ed sosyedad tan ekonomiya. Diad saray sinmublay ya dekada, walay pananguman ed kayarian na dalin, panagdalus, edukasyon, tan saray organisasyon ed komunidad.

english: After the war, Mapandan’s communities began to take shape. New barangays were formed, land ownership changed hands, and the municipality entered a period of organized community development.
pangasinan: Kalpasan na guerra, ginmapo so panagduruman na saray komunidad na Mapandan. Wala lay balon barangay, nanuman so kayarian na dalin, tan ginmapo so organisadon panagpaaligwas na komunidad.

english: Instead of only telling municipal history, the history of how Mapandan’s communities formed tells an equally important story.
pangasinan: Aliwa labat ya say awaran na munisipalidad so importante ya ibaga; importante met so awaran na impanmorma na saray komunidad ed Mapandan.

english: — Formerly part of Luyan, developed from former hacienda land. Tenants gained opportunities to own the land they had been farming after the war. It became a separate barrio in 1965.
pangasinan: — Datin parte na Luyan, ya nanmorma manlapud dalin na daan ya hacienda. Kalpasan na guerra, akapagana iray managdalus ya makayari ed dalin ya dadalusen da. Nagin bukod ya barrio nen 1965.

english: — Formerly Amanoaoac North, a sitio of Amanoaoac. Its name was associated with the Golden Distillery, which operated after liberation. Golden became a separate barangay in 1967.
pangasinan: — Dati ya Amanoaoac North, sakey ya sitio na Amanoaoac. Say ngaran to et nianam ed Golden Distillery ya nag-operasyon kalpasan na liberasyon. Nagin bukod ya barangay so Golden nen 1967.

english: — The first seat of Mapandan, which once contained several sitios that later developed into separate barangays.
pangasinan: — Say inmunan sentro na Mapandan, ya walaan na pigaran sitio ya nagmaliw ya bukod-bukod ya barangay ed saman ya panaon.

english: Golden was officially approved as a separate barangay in 1967. The community then underwent substantial development including road improvement, waterworks, school construction, sports facilities, cooperative organization, agricultural training, and sanitation programs.
pangasinan: Opisyal ya inaprobaran so Golden bilang bukod ya barangay nen 1967. Insan, baleg so inaligwas na komunidad, kaiba so panangpaaligwas ed dalan, sistema na danum, panangipaalagey na eskuela, pasilidad ed isport, kooperatiba, panagsanay ed panagdalus, tan saray programa ed kalinisan.

english: — Golden was recognized as a SEATO/PACD Model Village, receiving a national-level award presented in Malacañang on September 8, 1972.
pangasinan: — Nikilala so Golden bilang SEATO/PACD Model Village, tan angawat na pambansan premyo ya initer ed Malacañang nen Setyembre 8, 1972.

english: Mapandan’s population grew substantially, its services expanded, and infrastructure developed. The municipality moved from historical survival toward economic growth.
pangasinan: Baleg so inlakel na populasyon na Mapandan, dinmakel iray serbisyo, tan inaligwas so imprastruktura. Manlapud saray pagsubok ed awaran, ginmapo so panagduruman na ekonomiya na baley.

english: Mapandan’s population grew steadily through the second half of the 20th century: 20,094 in 1980, 25,622 in 1990, and 30,775 in 2000.
pangasinan: Tuloy-tuloy so inlakel na populasyon na Mapandan diad komadua ya kalahati na komadalawam ya siglo: 20,094 nen 1980, 25,622 nen 1990, tan 30,775 nen 2000.

english: The municipality expanded roads, schools, health facilities, and public services. Community organizations grew alongside the population.
pangasinan: Pinapalak so saray dalan, eskuela, pasilidad ed salun-at, tan publikon serbisyo na munisipalidad. Dinmakel met so saray organisasyon ed komunidad kasabay na populasyon.

english: From a new municipal classification to healthcare expansion and digital government—Mapandan enters the 21st century with growing services, cultural pride, and a more connected community.
pangasinan: Manlapud balon klasipikasyon na munisipalidad anggad ed panagpalak na serbisyo ed salun-at tan digital ya gobyerno—sinmabi so Mapandan ed komadalawam tan sakey ya siglo ya onlalak so serbisyo, pagmamalaki ed kultura, tan mas makapankonekta ya komunidad.

english: Mapandan was elevated to a third-class municipality. The municipality credits then-Mayor Jose Ferdinand Z. Calimlim Jr. with spearheading income and revenue-generation strategies that contributed to the municipality’s elevation.
pangasinan: Nagnaliw so Mapandan bilang komatlon klase ya munisipalidad. Inkilala na munisipalidad so panangidaulo nen datin Mayor Jose Ferdinand Z. Calimlim Jr. ed saray paraan ya nangpapalak ed kita tan nangitulong ed panagtaas na klasipikasyon.

english: The Pandan Festival developed into an important annual celebration of Mapandan’s identity, culture and community. The 9th Pandan Festival was held alongside the town fiesta from March 11–19, 2018.
pangasinan: Nagmaliw ya importantin tinawon selebrasyon na identidad, kultura, tan komunidad na Mapandan so Pandan Festival. Inselebra so komasiyam ya Pandan Festival kasabay na pista na baley nen Marso 11–19, 2018.

english: The municipal government began developing an online presence that made government information, public notices, disaster information and community announcements accessible through the web.
pangasinan: Inggapo na gobyerno na munisipalidad so panangipagawa na online ya paraan pian maligen ya nanengneng ed internet so impormasyon na gobyerno, publikon abiso, impormasyon ed kalamidad, tan saray anunsio parad komunidad.

english: National health infrastructure funding supported the development of the Mapandan Super Health Center. The 2022 General Appropriations Act included ₱6.5 million for the project. Its first phase was inaugurated on March 15, 2024, expanding access to laboratory, dental and primary healthcare services for residents of Mapandan and nearby communities.
pangasinan: Tinulongan na pambansan pondo parad imprastruktura ed salun-at so panagpaaligwas na Mapandan Super Health Center. Diad General Appropriations Act na 2022, wala so ₱6.5 milyon parad proyekto. Inagyan na seremonya so inmunan yugto nen Marso 15, 2024, pian mas ma-access so laboratoryo, serbisyo ed ngipen, tan manunan serbisyo ed salun-at na saray taga-Mapandan tan asingger ya komunidad.

english: Mapandan is a third-class municipality in the province of Pangasinan, Philippines. It covers a land area of 32.92 km² and is composed of 15 barangays. english: More than 130 years after its establishment as a pueblo, Mapandan is a 15-barangay municipality with a population of 38,228. Its history has been shaped by migration, agriculture, community organization, local government, cultural traditions and continuing investment in public services.
